Three title sets in this Phase-1 file: cuv (simplified), cuv-tr (traditional), english-classic (English). The version-to-set mapping lives in lib/constants/section_title_map.dart.

1.title: 起初创造天地
1.context: 圣经的开篇，回应人类最古老的问题：宇宙、生命、人类从何而来？

2.title: 伊甸园
2.context: 镜头从宇宙拉近到伊甸园：人是按神的形象造的，被安置在乐园中、与神同在。

3.title: 人类的堕落
3.context: 人类故事的转折：受造物的悖逆，破坏了与神、与人、与受造界的关系。

4.title: 该隐与亚伯
4.context: 亚当离开伊甸园外的第一个家庭：兄弟相残，是堕落最早的果效之一。

6.title: 挪亚造方舟
6.context: 人类败坏到极点，神选择以洪水洗净大地，但通过挪亚保留人类的指望。

7.title: 洪水来到
7.context: 神的审判与拯救并存：洪水洗净大地，但方舟保全挪亚一家，预表更大的救赎。

11.title: 巴别塔
11.context: 人类企图自筑通天高塔，宣告自主与团结，却招致语言的混乱与分散。

12.title: 神呼召亚伯兰
12.context: 圣经核心的转折：神呼召一个人——亚伯兰，借他祝福万族。这是救赎史的开端。

14.title: 麦基洗德祝福亚伯兰
14.context: 「至高神的祭司」麦基洗德接受亚伯拉罕的十一奉献——希伯来书第七章详述他预表基督。

15.title: 神与亚伯兰立约
15.context: 神的立约异象：神「自下而过」，独自承担违约的咒诅，预示基督担当我们的罪。

17.title: 立割礼之约
17.context: 割礼之约——身体上的印记，标记神立约之民的身份。后世保罗指出真割礼是心里的。

18.title: 亚伯拉罕为所多玛代求

19.title: 所多玛与蛾摩拉的毁灭
19.context: 所多玛的毁灭——圣经中最著名的审判事件之一，也是新约屡次提及的警戒。

21.title: 以撒出生
21.context: 二十五年后的应许成就：以撒出生。神的应许从不落空，只是按祂的时间。

22.title: 亚伯拉罕献以撒
22.context: 亚伯拉罕信心的最终试炼，预表父神献子救赎人类的伟大爱。

28.title: 雅各在伯特利的梦
28.context: 雅各逃亡的第一夜在旷野枕石而眠，却梦见天梯——耶稣在约翰福音1:51 引用。

32.title: 雅各与神摔跤
32.context: 雅各在雅博渡口与神角力，得新名「以色列」，亦得跛行——伤痕成为他一生的祝福记号。

37.title: 约瑟被卖
37.context: 约瑟被亲兄弟出卖到埃及，神却用人的恶意成就拯救——日后保全了雅各家族。

39.title: 约瑟在波提乏家
39.context: 约瑟的人生从私室到深井再到囚牢，神「与他同在」始终未变——一个从不放弃的应许。

45.title: 约瑟与兄弟相认
45.context: 二十年的分离与误会，化为兄弟流泪相拥。约瑟从不诅咒兄弟，反而看见神的护理。

50.title: 约瑟安慰兄弟
50.context: 约瑟说：「你们的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的。」饶恕的最高典范。

3.title: 燃烧的荆棘
3.context: 燃烧而不烧毁的荆棘——四十年寂静后神向摩西显现，开启出埃及的故事。

12.title: 逾越节设立
12.context: 逾越节的设立——羔羊的血涂在门上，神「越过」以色列家。预表基督被钉的那夜。

14.title: 过红海
14.context: 过红海——出埃及救赎的高峰。法老追兵在后，红海在前，神开道路。

19.title: 在西奈山立约
19.context: 西奈山——神向以色列显现立约的地点。从此他们成为「祭司的国度，圣洁的国民」。

20.title: 颁布十诫
20.context: 十诫——神立约关系的核心：先表明祂的拯救，再赐下顺服祂的方式。

25.title: 会幕与约柜的样式
25.context: 会幕的设计——神要住在祂百姓中间。每一个细节都预表更美的「圣所」（基督和教会）。

32.title: 金牛犊事件
32.context: 金牛犊事件——摩西在山上四十天，山下百姓已离弃神。圣经核心叛逆事件之一。

40.title: 立起会幕、神荣光充满
40.context: 出埃及记的高峰：神的荣光充满会幕。神实在与祂的百姓同住——主题贯穿整本圣经。

16.title: 赎罪日
16.context: 赎罪日——以色列圣历中最庄严的一天。两只山羊：一献为祭，一被赶到旷野作替罪羊。

19.title: 圣洁的法则
19.context: 「你们要圣洁，因为我耶和华你们的神是圣洁的」——利未记的核心，彼得前书1:16 直接引用。

13.title: 十二探子
13.context: 十二探子的报告：十人传恶信、二人凭信靠。一代以色列因不信而失去应许之地。

21.title: 铜蛇的事件
21.context: 铜蛇的事件——耶稣在约翰福音3:14 引用此事，预示祂自己被举起。

6.title: 示玛——爱耶和华
6.context: 示玛——「以色列啊你要听！」每个虔诚犹太人每日的宣告。耶稣称之为「最大的诫命」。

30.title: 悔改与归回
30.context: 悔改与归回——出埃及记的高潮——神应许在被掳之后将祂的子民重新带回，赐他们新心。

1.title: 神呼召约书亚
1.context: 摩西去世后，约书亚承接领导。神三次重复「刚强壮胆」——一句使他能面对未知的应许。

2.title: 喇合与探子
2.context: 喇合是耶利哥城的妓女，却因信加入神的子民——基督家谱中的第一位外邦女子。

5.title: 在吉甲行割礼与守逾越节

6.title: 耶利哥城倒塌
6.context: 耶利哥城的城墙倒塌——以色列以「七天围城、围圈呼喊」战胜，靠的是神，不是兵器。

24.title: 在示剑立约
24.context: 约书亚在示剑发出最后挑战：「至于我和我家，我们必定事奉耶和华。」

4.title: 底波拉与巴拉
4.context: 底波拉——士师中唯一的女先知，与雅亿一同打败迦南强敌西西拉。

6.title: 基甸蒙召
6.context: 基甸——一个胆怯的农夫，神称他为「大能的勇士」。神所看见的，远超我们所是。

1.title: 路得忠心的誓言
1.context: 「你的国就是我的国，你的神就是我的神」——一位摩押女子立誓向以色列的神，加入立约之家。

2.title: 路得在波阿斯田中拾穗

4.title: 俄备得出生与大卫家谱

1.title: 撒母耳的出生
1.context: 哈拿不孕之痛与切切的祷告——撒母耳的诞生应验了神听见破碎之心的应许。

3.title: 撒母耳蒙召
3.context: 「主啊请说，仆人敬听」——少年撒母耳的回应，成为历世历代敬虔者的祷告范本。

8.title: 百姓求立王
8.context: 百姓求一个人间的王——他们拒绝的不是撒母耳，而是神祂自己。神依然祝福，但有警戒。

16.title: 膏立大卫
16.context: 神拣选最小的儿子大卫——「人是看外貌，耶和华是看内心」。圣经最重要的拣选原则之一。

17.title: 大卫与歌利亚
17.context: 大卫与歌利亚——一个少年凭信靠神击败巨人，成为以色列乃至历世历代信心的象征。

1.title: 大卫为扫罗约拿单哀歌

7.title: 大卫之约
7.context: 大卫之约——神应许大卫的王位永远长存。所有弥赛亚预言的源头，新约称耶稣为「大卫的子孙」即在此。

11.title: 大卫与拔示巴
11.context: 大卫的最大失败——与拔示巴犯罪并谋杀乌利亚。圣经从不美化英雄；它告诉真相。

21.title: 三年饥荒与大卫的勇士

23.title: 大卫的临终之言与勇士

3.title: 所罗门求智慧
3.context: 所罗门求智慧而非财富——成为后世数千年「祈求得当」的典范。

11.title: 所罗门的妻子使他离开神

14.title: 亚希雅预言耶罗波安家

18.title: 迦密山上的对决
18.context: 迦密山的对决——以利亚单独面对四百五十名巴力先知。神以火回应，百姓宣告：「耶和华是神！」

19.title: 以利亚逃到何烈山
19.context: 迦密山大胜后，以利亚却陷入忧郁。神以「微小的声音」陪伴他——疲惫的事奉者读了都得安慰。

2.title: 以利亚被接升天
2.context: 以利亚乘旋风升天——只有以诺与他在圣经中未尝死亡。以利沙得双倍的灵承接事工。

5.title: 乃缦得医
5.context: 亚兰大将乃缦因长大痲疯而忍辱在约旦河浸七次得医——预表外邦人也得救恩。

1.title: 亚当至亚伯拉罕的家谱

5.title: 流便、迦得、玛拿西半支派

9.title: 回归后的耶路撒冷居民
以斯拉为百姓的罪悲哀

1.title: 尼希米为耶路撒冷祷告
义人与恶人之路
1.context: 诗篇的开篇，定下整卷书的基调：默想神律法的人有福，恶人必如糠秕被风吹散。

2.title: 弥赛亚君王
2.context: 弥赛亚君王诗篇，被新约多次引用，描绘列国敌挡神受膏者的徒然。

8.title: 神荣耀与人尊贵
8.context: 在浩瀚星空之下默想：「人算什么？你竟眷顾他？」希伯来书第二章引用此节描述基督。

22.title: 受苦者的呼求
22.context: 「我的神！我的神！为什么离弃我？」——耶稣在十字架上引用的诗篇，预表受苦的弥赛亚。

23.title: 耶和华是我的牧者
23.context: 全圣经最为人熟知的诗篇之一。在死荫幽谷与生命平安之间，宣告耶和华是牧者。

27.title: 耶和华是我的亮光
27.context: 「耶和华是我的亮光，是我的拯救，我还怕谁呢？」——黑暗中的信心宣告。

37.title: 不要为作恶者心怀不平

42.title: 如鹿渴慕溪水
42.context: 「我的心切慕你，如鹿切慕溪水。」忧郁中的诗人，仍指着神说话。

46.title: 神是我们的避难所
46.context: 「神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。」马丁路德的「坚固保障」赞美诗源自此。

51.title: 悔罪诗
51.context: 大卫与拔示巴犯罪后的悔罪诗。每个跌倒、却仍盼望神饶恕者都能在此找到自己。

90.title: 神是永远的居所
90.context: 摩西所作的诗——感叹人生的短暂，求神「使我们得着智慧的心」。

91.title: 至高者的隐密处
91.context: 投靠至高者的人有特殊保护的应许——魔鬼在试探耶稣时也曾错引此诗。

100.title: 感恩之歌
100.context: 向耶和华唱新歌——欢乐颂赞之诗，西方教会千年来在崇拜中颂唱。

106.title: 神的恩慈与百姓的悖逆

118.title: 感恩诗：耶和华的恩慈永远长存

119.title: 神话语的诗篇
119.context: 圣经中最长的一章。22 个段落，按希伯来字母为顺序，全篇默想神的话语。

121.title: 我的帮助从何而来
121.context: 「我的帮助从何而来？我的帮助从造天地的耶和华而来。」上行之诗的代表。

130.title: 深渊中呼求
130.context: 「我从深处向你求告」——悔罪诗篇的核心，路德称之为「保罗式诗篇」。

139.title: 神无所不知无所不在
139.context: 对神无所不知、无所不在最深刻的反思。即使到地极、到阴间，神仍紧紧握住我们。

150.title: 用各样乐器赞美神
150.context: 诗篇的最后一首——纯粹的颂赞。从最深的哀歌（诗22）到最高的赞美（诗150），一切都归于祂。

1.title: 智慧的开端：敬畏耶和华

31.title: 利慕伊勒王之母的训诲
才德的妇人
31.context: 才德妇人——希伯来文按字母离合诗写成，是箴言对家庭与生活智慧的总结。

3.title: 凡事都有定时
3.context: 「凡事都有定时」——人生节奏的诗篇，提醒我们神在万有之上。

12.title: 记念你的造物主
12.context: 全卷的高峰：在年轻时记念创造主。诗意地描绘衰老与死亡。

6.title: 以赛亚蒙召
6.context: 以赛亚见到神坐在宝座上——一次彻底改变其一生的异象。也启发了「圣哉、圣哉、圣哉」的颂歌。

9.title: 为我们生了一婴孩
9.context: 「因有一婴孩为我们而生……他名称为奇妙策士、全能的神、永在的父、和平的君」。圣诞经文之一。

11.title: 弥赛亚的国
11.context: 弥赛亚君王从「耶西的根」长出——日后以赛亚再三回到这棵君王的「枝子」。

40.title: 我的百姓哪，要得安慰
40.context: 以赛亚书第二部分的开场——「我的百姓哪，要得安慰！」从审判转入安慰。新约以此宣告施洗约翰。

53.title: 受苦仆人
53.context: 在公元前700年所写的代赎预言——耶稣的钉痕、被弃、为我们的过犯受害，每一句都映照各各他。

65.title: 新天新地
65.context: 「看哪，我造新天新地」——指向启示录21章。圣经最大的盼望首先在以赛亚发声。

1.title: 耶利米蒙召
1.context: 耶利米被神拣选「在腹中尚未成形」之时——历世历代呼召年轻人事奉的有力提醒。

31.title: 新约的预言
31.context: 新约的预言——希伯来书第八章直接引用，证其在基督里得着应验。

3.title: 他的慈爱永不止息
3.context: 在国家最大的悲剧中央，先知发出最伟大的恩典宣告：「他的怜悯不止息」。

36.title: 新心与新灵
36.context: 「我要赐给你们一颗新心，将新灵放在你们里面」——五旬节圣灵降临的预表。

37.title: 枯骨复活的异象
37.context: 枯骨复活的异象——一个被毁灭的国家如何能重生？神说，借着祂的话语和祂的灵。

3.title: 火窑中的三人
3.context: 三个犹太青年宁死也不拜金像——「即或不然」的信心：神能救我们，但即使祂不救，我们仍信。

6.title: 但以理在狮子坑中
6.context: 但以理在狮子坑中——晚年仍然每日三次面向耶路撒冷祷告。忠贞胜过自保。

7.title: 四兽与人子
7.context: 「人子」乘云而来——但以理见到基督最深的预表。耶稣最常用的自称即出此处。

9.title: 但以理的祷告与七十个七
9.context: 但以理逐字读耶利米的预言而醒悟——这位先知教我们如何因圣经的应许而祷告。

2.title: 对犹大与以色列的审判

1.title: 约拿逃避使命
1.context: 约拿不是逃避使命，而是逃避神的怜悯——他不愿尼尼微悔改。圣经中最诚实的先知。

3.title: 向尼尼微传道
3.context: 尼尼微全城悔改——耶稣称约拿的事工为祂复活的预表（太12:40）。

1.title: 对撒玛利亚与犹大的审判

5.title: 伯利恒的应许
5.context: 在被掳的阴影下，弥迦预言伯利恒——基督出生的小镇。希律王的祭司在马太福音2章引用此节。

1.title: 耶和华是慈爱也是公义

2.title: 义人因信得生
2.context: 「义人必因信得生」——新约引用三次，是宗教改革的根基经文。

3.title: 耶路撒冷的审判与复兴

9.title: 君王骑驴而来
9.context: 「看哪，你的王来到！谦谦和和地骑着驴」——预言500年后耶稣骑驴进耶路撒冷。

4.title: 公义的日头
4.context: 旧约的最后预言：以利亚要再来。施洗约翰来履行这预言（太11:14）。然后是400年的沉默。

1.title: 耶稣的家谱
1.context: 马太福音以耶稣的家谱开篇，证明祂是亚伯拉罕之子（应许）与大卫之子（君王）。

5.title: 登山宝训：八福
5.context: 耶稣事工初期最重要的讲论，颠覆人对「有福」的理解：贫穷、哀恸、饥渴慕义之人——这些人有福了。

5.title: 盐与光
5.context: 盐与光——耶稣对门徒身份的核心宣告。这不是命令，而是事实：你们已经是。

6.title: 主祷文
6.context: 耶稣亲自教导门徒祷告。每一句都是天国子民与天父关系的核心。

6.title: 论忧虑
6.context: 「不要忧虑」——耶稣三次重复这句话。天父养活地上的飞鸟，岂不更照顾你？

13.title: 撒种的比喻
13.context: 天国的比喻：耶稣以日常生活的图画启示天国的奥秘。第七章是教师；这里是讲故事的人。

14.title: 喂饱五千人
14.context: 在听到施洗约翰被斩首的消息后，耶稣退到旷野却被群众跟随——祂以五饼二鱼喂饱五千人。

16.title: 彼得的认信
16.context: 彼得在该撒利亚腓立比认信耶稣是基督，是神的儿子——四福音事工的转折点。

17.title: 耶稣登山变像

21.title: 光荣进入耶路撒冷

25.title: 羊与山羊
25.context: 末日审判的画面——耶稣按我们如何对待「祂的弟兄中最小的」来审判。

26.title: 最后的晚餐
26.context: 耶稣最后的逾越节晚餐，设立圣餐礼。祂的身体与血即将作为新约的祭。

26.title: 客西马尼园祷告
26.context: 客西马尼园的祷告：耶稣以人性面对受难的恐惧，仍顺服天父的旨意。

27.title: 钉十字架
27.context: 钉十字架——历史上最公开的处决。圣经四卷福音以此为高峰，用最少的笔墨描述最大的事件。

28.title: 耶稣复活
28.context: 整本新约的高潮：耶稣从死里复活，证实祂的牺牲获蒙天父悦纳，开启永恒的盼望。

28.title: 大使命

5.context: 睚鲁的女儿与血漏妇人——两个绝望的故事相互交织：一位会堂主管的女儿与一位被社会遗弃的妇女。

彼得的认信

9.title: 耶稣登山变像
9.context: 登山变像——耶稣在山上向三位门徒短暂展现祂神性的荣光，与摩西、以利亚同立。

14.title: 客西马尼园祷告
14.context: 客西马尼园祷告——完全的人性面对受苦的恐惧，却仍说：「不要照我的意思，只要照你的意思。」

16.title: 耶稣复活
16.context: 基督教信仰的根基：耶稣从死里复活。马可的简短记述充满了亲历目击者的细节。

2.title: 耶稣降生伯利恒
2.context: 耶稣的降生——在罗马帝国的人口普查中，弥赛亚生于伯利恒的客店外。神的故事在历史中。

4.title: 受试探
4.context: 耶稣受洗后立即被引到旷野受试探——四十天对应以色列人四十年。第二个亚当在魔鬼面前胜利。

10.title: 好撒玛利亚人的比喻
10.context: 好撒玛利亚人的比喻——耶稣破除种族偏见，定义「邻舍」是任何有需要的人。

15.title: 失羊、失钱、浪子
15.context: 三个失而复得的比喻——失羊、失钱、浪子——教导神主动寻找、欢喜接纳的心。

24.title: 以马忤斯路上
24.context: 以马忤斯路上——两位灰心的门徒在路上遇见复活的主，回顾整本旧约都指向祂。

3.context: 尼哥底母夜访耶稣，听见震撼一生的话：「人若不重生，就不能见神的国。」

4.title: 撒玛利亚妇人
4.context: 耶稣超越种族、性别、宗教的偏见，向一位撒玛利亚妇女启示自己是「活水」。

6.title: 喂饱五千人
6.context: 喂饱五千人——四福音都记载的唯一神迹（除复活外）。约翰用这事件展开「我是生命的粮」的讲论。

8.title: 行淫的妇人
8.context: 行淫的妇人被带到耶稣面前——「你们中间谁是没有罪的，谁就可以先拿石头打她。」

9.title: 医治生来瞎眼的人
9.context: 生来瞎眼的人得医——但故事的高峰不是身体的得医，而是属灵眼睛的开启。

10.title: 好牧人
10.context: 「我是好牧人」——耶稣引用以西结34章对失败牧者的责备，宣告自己来作真牧人。

11.title: 拉撒路复活
11.context: 约翰福音最戏剧性的神迹：耶稣使死了四天的拉撒路复活，预先彰显祂自己的复活权能。

13.title: 为门徒洗脚
13.context: 最后晚餐前，耶稣亲自为门徒洗脚——颠覆所有关于权力和事奉的世俗观念。

14.title: 我是道路、真理、生命
14.context: 最后的晚餐之夜，耶稣以爱心安慰惊惶的门徒：「我就是道路、真理、生命。」

15.title: 真葡萄树
15.context: 「我是真葡萄树」——耶稣以以色列经常的形象（葡萄树）描绘信徒与祂之间的生命联合。

17.title: 耶稣大祭司的祷告
17.context: 耶稣大祭司的祷告——为门徒、为后世信徒祈求，是新约最深的祷告。

20.title: 空坟墓

2.context: 五旬节圣灵降临，应验耶稣的应许。从这一刻起，教会诞生，不分种族、地域。

8.title: 腓利与埃塞俄比亚太监
8.context: 腓利与埃塞俄比亚太监——福音首次明确传给非洲。一个外邦官长读以赛亚53章而归主。

9.title: 扫罗大马士革路上的归正

彼得医治以尼雅与多加复活

10.context: 彼得到外邦百夫长哥尼流家——福音正式打开外邦的门。

16.title: 吕底亚信主
16.context: 吕底亚信主——欧洲教会的第一颗种子。一位经商的妇人，全家受洗，成立腓立比教会。

17.title: 亚略巴古的讲道
17.context: 保罗在雅典亚略巴古的讲道——向异教知识分子宣讲创造主、悔改与复活。

13.context: 爱的篇章——婚礼中常诵读，但本是写给一间分裂的教会，提醒爱才是真属灵的标志。

4.context: 瓦器中的宝贝——保罗最深刻的事工自画像：脆弱的器皿盛装永恒的荣耀。

1.title: 试炼中得喜乐

3.title: 舌头的危险
3.context: 舌头的危险——雅各以鲜明的图画警告言语的杀伤力：火、毒、不可驯服的舌头。

2.context: 「你们是被拣选的族类、有君尊的祭司」——出埃及记19章对以色列的话语，如今给教会。

4.context: 「不要以试炼为奇怪的事」——苦难是基督徒生活的一部分，不是反常。彼得本人深知此事。

4.context: 「神就是爱」——圣经中对神本性最深刻的两句话之一（另一处是约翰福音4:24「神是灵」）。

1.title: 向七教会启示
1.context: 启示录开篇——在拔摩岛被流放的约翰得到异象，揭开宇宙历史的帷幕。

4.context: 天上的宝座异象——一切混乱与失败的世界以下，神依然作王。崇拜的中心。

5.title: 羔羊揭开书卷
5.context: 羔羊揭开七印——「曾被杀的羔羊」是唯一配开书卷的，宇宙历史的钥匙。

19.title: 白马骑士
19.context: 白马骑士——基督的得胜归回。新约的第一画面是马槽，最后画面是宝座。

21.title: 新天新地
21.context: 「新天新地」——圣经最大的盼望应验。神与子民同住，再没有眼泪、死亡、痛苦。

22.title: 我必快来
22.context: 圣经最后的应许：「我必快来！」教会两千年来的回应：「主耶稣啊，我愿祢来！」

1.title: 起初創造天地
1.context: 聖經的開篇，回應人類最古老的問題：宇宙、生命、人類從何而來？

2.context: 鏡頭從宇宙拉近到伊甸園：人是按神的形象造的，被安置在樂園中、與神同在。

3.context: 人類故事的轉折：受造物的悖逆，破壞了與神、與人、與受造界的關係。

4.context: 亞當離開伊甸園外的第一個家庭：兄弟相殘，是墮落最早的果效之一。

6.title: 挪亞造方舟
6.context: 人類敗壞到極點，神選擇以洪水洗淨大地，但通過挪亞保留人類的指望。

7.title: 洪水來到
7.context: 神的審判與拯救並存：洪水洗淨大地，但方舟保全挪亞一家，預表更大的救贖。

11.title: 巴別塔
11.context: 人類企圖自築通天高塔，宣告自主與團結，卻招致語言的混亂與分散。

12.title: 神呼召亞伯蘭
12.context: 聖經核心的轉折：神呼召一個人——亞伯蘭，藉他祝福萬族。這是救贖史的開端。

17.context: 割禮之約——身體上的印記，標記神立約之民的身份。後世保羅指出真割禮是心裡的。

18.title: 亞伯拉罕為所多瑪代求

19.title: 所多瑪與蛾摩拉的毀滅
19.context: 所多瑪的毀滅——聖經中最著名的審判事件之一，也是新約屢次提及的警戒。

21.title: 以撒出生
21.context: 二十五年後的應許成就：以撒出生。神的應許從不落空，只是按祂的時間。

22.context: 亞伯拉罕信心的最終試煉，預表父神獻子救贖人類的偉大愛。

3.title: 燃燒的荊棘

19.title: 在西奈山立約

20.title: 頒布十誡

10.context: 好撒瑪利亞人的比喻——耶穌破除種族偏見，定義「鄰舍」是任何有需要的人。

15.title: 失羊、失錢、浪子
15.context: 三個失而復得的比喻——失羊、失錢、浪子——教導神主動尋找、歡喜接納的心。

18.title: 不義官與法利賽人稅吏

19.title: 撒該
19.context: 撒該是耶利哥的稅吏長，被人輕視。耶穌主動到他家——「人子來為要尋找拯救失喪的人。」

24.title: 以馬忤斯路上
24.context: 以馬忤斯路上——兩位灰心的門徒在路上遇見復活的主，回顧整本舊約都指向祂。

1.title: 道成肉身
1.context: 約翰福音以創世記為鏡像開篇——那位在起初就有的「道」，如今成了肉身。

3.title: 尼哥底母訪耶穌
3.context: 尼哥底母夜訪耶穌，聽見震撼一生的話：「人若不重生，就不能見神的國。」

4.title: 撒瑪利亞婦人
4.context: 耶穌超越種族、性別、宗教的偏見，向一位撒瑪利亞婦女啟示自己是「活水」。

6.title: 餵飽五千人
6.context: 餵飽五千人——四福音都記載的唯一神蹟（除復活外）。約翰用這事件展開「我是生命的糧」的講論。

8.title: 行淫的婦人
8.context: 行淫的婦人被帶到耶穌面前——「你們中間誰是沒有罪的，誰就可以先拿石頭打她。」

9.title: 醫治生來瞎眼的人
9.context: 生來瞎眼的人得醫——但故事的高峰不是身體的得醫，而是屬靈眼睛的開啟。

10.title: 好牧人
10.context: 「我是好牧人」——耶穌引用以西結34章對失敗牧者的責備，宣告自己來作真牧人。

11.title: 拉撒路復活
11.context: 約翰福音最戲劇性的神蹟：耶穌使死了四天的拉撒路復活，預先彰顯祂自己的復活權能。

13.title: 為門徒洗腳
13.context: 最後晚餐前，耶穌親自為門徒洗腳——顛覆所有關於權力和事奉的世俗觀念。

14.title: 我是道路、真理、生命
14.context: 最後的晚餐之夜，耶穌以愛心安慰驚惶的門徒：「我就是道路、真理、生命。」

15.title: 真葡萄樹
15.context: 「我是真葡萄樹」——耶穌以以色列經常的形象（葡萄樹）描繪信徒與祂之間的生命聯合。

17.title: 耶穌大祭司的禱告
17.context: 耶穌大祭司的禱告——為門徒、為後世信徒祈求，是新約最深的禱告。

20.title: 空墳墓
20.context: 空墳墓——基督教信仰的根基。約翰冷靜地記錄他親眼所見的細節。

20.title: 向抹大拉的馬利亞顯現

1.title: 耶穌升天前的應許
1.context: 使徒行傳是路加福音的續集——耶穌升天後，聖靈藉門徒展開教會的擴展史。

2.title: 聖靈降臨
2.context: 五旬節聖靈降臨，應驗耶穌的應許。從這一刻起，教會誕生，不分種族、地域。

7.title: 司提反殉道
7.context: 司提反殉道——教會史上第一位殉道者。在他被石頭打死之時，掃羅（保羅）在旁觀看。

8.title: 腓利與埃塞俄比亞太監
8.context: 腓利與埃塞俄比亞太監——福音首次明確傳給非洲。一個外邦官長讀以賽亞53章而歸主。

9.title: 掃羅大馬士革路上的歸正
9.context: 教會最大的逼迫者掃羅（保羅）在大馬士革路上遇見復活的主——歷史的轉折點。

9.title: 掃羅在大馬士革與耶路撒冷傳道
彼得醫治以尼雅與多加復活

10.title: 哥尼流的異象
10.context: 彼得到外邦百夫長哥尼流家——福音正式打開外邦的門。

11.title: 彼得在耶路撒冷的報告

12.title: 希律殺害雅各囚禁彼得

15.title: 耶路撒冷會議
15.context: 耶路撒冷會議：教會決定外邦信徒不必受割禮。這定義了教會的合一與多元。

16.title: 呂底亞信主
16.context: 呂底亞信主——歐洲教會的第一顆種子。一位經商的婦人，全家受洗，成立腓立比教會。

17.title: 亞略巴古的講道
17.context: 保羅在雅典亞略巴古的講道——向異教知識分子宣講創造主、悔改與復活。

18.title: 回安提阿與第三次旅程

20.title: 在特羅亞使猶推古復活

23.title: 保羅被解送至該撒利亞

26.title: 保羅在亞基帕前的辯論

27.title: 前往羅馬的航程
27.context: 保羅向羅馬的航行——一位囚犯在大風暴中成為眾水手的安慰。最準確的古代航海記述之一。

1.title: 福音的大能
1.context: 保羅的論文起點：「我不以福音為恥」。整卷書是這一句的展開。

3.title: 因信稱義
3.context: 羅馬書的核心：因信稱義。神在律法以外向世人顯明祂自己的義。

5.title: 因信得平安
5.context: 因信稱義的果效：與神和好、得享平安、進入恩典、誇耀盼望——也包括苦難帶來的成長。

8.title: 聖靈的生命
8.context: 羅馬書的最高峰之一。「在基督耶穌裡的就不定罪了」——並以「萬事互相效力」收尾。

12.title: 活祭與新生
12.context: 保羅從「神為我們做了什麼」轉到「我們當如何回應」——將身體獻作活祭，是合理的事奉。

11.title: 聖餐的意義
11.context: 聖餐的意義——保羅修正哥林多教會濫用主餐的問題：聖餐是「宣告主的死，直等到祂來」。

13.title: 愛的篇章
13.context: 愛的篇章——婚禮中常誦讀，但本是寫給一間分裂的教會，提醒愛才是真屬靈的標誌。

15.title: 復活的真理
15.context: 復活的章節——基督教信仰的根基。「若基督沒有復活，你們的信便是徒然」。

4.title: 瓦器中的寶貝
4.context: 瓦器中的寶貝——保羅最深刻的事工自畫像：脆弱的器皿盛裝永恆的榮耀。

6.title: 不可與不信的同負一軛

12.title: 保羅的異象與肉中刺
12.context: 保羅的肉中刺——三次求神挪去都被拒絕。神說：「我的恩典夠你用的，因為我的能力是在人的軟弱上顯得完全。」

3.title: 聖靈與亞伯拉罕
3.context: 保羅以此向加拉太人發問：「你們這無知的加拉太人哪……」繼續闡明因信稱義的道理。

5.title: 聖靈的果子
5.context: 聖靈的果子——九重特質：仁愛、喜樂、和平、忍耐、恩慈、良善、信實、溫柔、節制。基督徒成長的標誌。

2.title: 本為死的我們活過來
2.context: 「你們死在過犯罪惡之中，祂叫你們活過來」——保羅最深刻地描述救恩從死到生的轉變。

6.title: 屬靈的軍裝
6.context: 屬靈的軍裝——基督徒不是在與人打仗，乃是與「天空屬靈氣的惡魔」爭戰。

2.title: 基督的謙卑榜樣
2.context: 基督頌歌——新約中關於耶穌身份與使命最濃縮的詩。可能是早期教會的讚美詩。

4.title: 凡事禱告交託
4.context: 「應當一無掛慮，只要凡事禱告」——保羅在監牢中所寫的喜樂宣告。

1.title: 基督的至高地位
1.context: 歌羅西基督頌歌——宣告基督是創造者、托住者、教會元首、萬有的和好者。

4.title: 我們的大祭司
4.context: 「我們的大祭司」——希伯來書的中心。耶穌完全體會我們的軟弱，又永遠活著為我們代求。

11.title: 信心的英雄
11.context: 「信心的英雄榜」——從亞伯到摩西，由舊約群聖構成。「這些人是世界不配有的」。

12.title: 仰望耶穌奔跑
12.context: 「奔那擺在我們前頭的路程」——希伯來書的牧養高峰。仰望耶穌，因祂忍受了十架。

1.title: 試煉中得喜樂
1.context: 雅各以「試煉當為大喜樂」開篇——顛覆人對苦難的理解：試煉成全信心。

2.title: 信心與行為
2.context: 「信心若沒有行為就是死的」——雅各的核心論點：補足、不是反駁保羅的因信稱義。

3.title: 舌頭的危險
3.context: 舌頭的危險——雅各以鮮明的圖畫警告言語的殺傷力：火、毒、不可馴服的舌頭。

1.title: 問候與活潑盼望
1.context: 彼得致信散居的「客旅」——基督徒的共同身份。我們的家不在此處，乃在天上。

2.title: 屬神的子民
2.context: 「你們是被揀選的族類、有君尊的祭司」——出埃及記19章對以色列的話語，如今給教會。

4.title: 火煉的考驗
4.context: 「不要以試煉為奇怪的事」——苦難是基督徒生活的一部分，不是反常。彼得本人深知此事。

3.title: 主再來與新天新地
3.context: 為何主遲遲不來？「主所應許的尚未成就……乃是寬容你們」。延遲即是憐憫。

4.title: 神就是愛
4.context: 「神就是愛」——聖經中對神本性最深刻的兩句話之一（另一處是約翰福音4:24「神是靈」）。

1.title: 向七教會啟示
1.context: 啟示錄開篇——在拔摩島被流放的約翰得到異象，揭開宇宙歷史的帷幕。

4.title: 天上的寶座
4.context: 天上的寶座異象——一切混亂與失敗的世界以下，神依然作王。崇拜的中心。

5.title: 羔羊揭開書卷
5.context: 羔羊揭開七印——「曾被殺的羔羊」是唯一配開書卷的，宇宙歷史的鑰匙。

19.title: 白馬騎士
19.context: 白馬騎士——基督的得勝歸回。新約的第一畫面是馬槽，最後畫面是寶座。

21.title: 新天新地
21.context: 「新天新地」——聖經最大的盼望應驗。神與子民同住，再沒有眼淚、死亡、痛苦。

22.title: 我必快來
22.context: 聖經最後的應許：「我必快來！」教會兩千年來的回應：「主耶穌啊，我願祢來！」

1.title: The Creation
1.context: The Bible opens with the most fundamental question: where did everything come from? The answer — God spoke it into being.

1.title: The Fourth Day: Sun, Moon, and Stars

2.title: The Garden of Eden
2.context: The camera zooms from cosmos to garden. The first humans are made in God's image and placed in fellowship with him.

3.title: The Fall of Mankind
3.context: The pivot of human history: a single act of distrust fractures every relationship — with God, with each other, with creation itself.

4.title: Cain and Abel
4.context: The first family outside Eden — and the first murder. Sin's poison spreads quickly: from disobedience in the garden to a brother killed in the field.

5.title: The Genealogy from Adam to Noah

6.title: Noah and the Ark
6.context: Mankind's wickedness has filled the earth. God will reset creation through a flood — but preserve a remnant through one righteous family.

7.title: The Great Flood
7.context: Judgment and salvation in one event: the flood cleanses the earth while the ark preserves Noah's family — a pattern Peter later sees as foreshadowing baptism.

11.title: The Tower of Babel
11.context: Humanity attempts to ascend to heaven by their own strength, defying God's command to fill the earth. The scattering of languages still shapes our world.

11.title: The Genealogy from Shem to Abram

12.title: The Call of Abram
12.context: The hinge of redemption history. God calls one man, Abram, promising to bless every nation through his line — a promise the rest of Scripture traces.

14.title: Melchizedek Blesses Abram
14.context: Melchizedek — 'priest of God Most High' — receives Abraham's tithe. Hebrews 7 spends an entire chapter on this brief encounter as a foretaste of Christ's priesthood.

15.title: God's Covenant with Abram
15.context: God seals his covenant by passing through the divided animals alone — taking on himself the curse of any breach. A breathtaking preview of Calvary.

17.title: The Covenant of Circumcision
17.context: The covenant of circumcision — a sign in the body marking God's covenant people. Paul will later teach that the true circumcision is of the heart.

19.title: The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
19.context: The destruction of Sodom — one of the Bible's most famous judgments, repeatedly cited in the New Testament as a warning of God's holiness.

21.title: The Birth of Isaac
21.context: Twenty-five years after the promise, Isaac is born. God's word never fails — but it operates on his timetable, not ours.

22.title: Abraham Offers Isaac
22.context: Abraham's ultimate test of faith. The scene of a father offering his only son on Mount Moriah foreshadows what God himself will one day do.

25.title: The Birth of Jacob and Esau

28.title: Jacob's Dream at Bethel
28.context: Fleeing for his life, Jacob dreams of a stairway joining heaven and earth. Jesus picks up this image in John 1:51 — saying he himself is the bridge.

32.title: Jacob Wrestles with God
32.context: Jacob wrestles with God at the Jabbok ford and emerges with a new name (Israel) and a permanent limp — a wound that becomes his lifelong sign of blessing.

37.title: Joseph Sold into Slavery
37.context: Sold by his own brothers into slavery, Joseph's story shows God working through human evil to preserve the covenant family.

39.title: Joseph in Potiphar's House
39.context: Joseph's life moves from pit to prison — yet at every stage, 'the LORD was with Joseph.' One unbroken thread through every reversal.

45.title: Joseph Reveals Himself
45.context: Twenty years of separation and silence collapse into tears and embrace. Joseph never curses his brothers — he sees God's providence behind every betrayal.

50.title: Joseph Reassures His Brothers
50.context: Joseph's famous declaration — 'You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good' — reframes decades of suffering as part of a redemptive plan.

3.title: The Burning Bush
3.context: After forty years of silence, God appears to Moses in a bush that burns without being consumed. The whole Exodus story begins here.

7.title: Aaron's Staff and the First Plague

12.title: The Passover Instituted
12.context: The Passover instituted — lamb's blood marks each home, and the angel of death 'passes over.' Jesus dies on Passover, fulfilling every detail.

14.title: Crossing the Red Sea
14.context: Crossing the Red Sea — the climax of the Exodus rescue. With Pharaoh's army behind and the sea ahead, God makes a way through impossibility.

19.title: At Mount Sinai
19.context: Mount Sinai — where the redeemed people meet their God to enter into covenant. They become 'a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.'

20.title: The Ten Commandments
20.context: The Ten Commandments — the heart of the covenant. God first declares his rescue ('I brought you out…'), then gives the shape of obedience that follows.

25.title: The Tabernacle and Ark
25.context: The tabernacle's design — God will dwell among his people. Every detail later finds fulfillment in Christ and his church (Heb 8-10).

32.title: The Golden Calf
32.context: The golden calf — while Moses is on the mountain, the people fashion a god they can see. One of Scripture's core stories of human idolatry.

40.title: The Glory Fills the Tabernacle
40.context: Exodus reaches its climax: God's glory fills the tabernacle. God really does dwell with his people — a thread that runs through every book of the Bible.

16.title: The Day of Atonement
16.context: The Day of Atonement — the most solemn day in Israel's calendar. Two goats: one sacrificed, one driven into the wilderness — both pictures of Christ's work.

19.title: Be Holy
19.context: 'Be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy.' The heart of Leviticus — quoted by Peter (1 Pet 1:16) as the church's calling.

13.title: Spies Sent into Canaan
13.context: The twelve spies — ten see giants, two see God. A whole generation forfeits the promised land because of unbelief at the threshold.

21.title: The Bronze Serpent
21.context: Snake-bitten Israelites look at the bronze serpent and live. Jesus picks up this story in John 3:14 to foreshadow his own being lifted up on the cross.

6.title: The Shema: Love the LORD
6.context: The Shema — 'Hear, O Israel.' The daily confession of every devout Jew. Jesus calls it the greatest commandment.

30.title: Return to the LORD
30.context: Even before the exile happens, God promises return. After judgment will come restoration — and a new heart that loves him.

1.title: God Commissions Joshua
1.context: After Moses' death, Joshua takes the lead. God says 'Be strong and courageous' three times — a promise that carries him through the unknown.

2.title: Rahab and the Spies
2.context: Rahab — a Canaanite prostitute — believes the rumors of YHWH and saves her family. She ends up in the genealogy of Jesus (Matt 1:5).

6.title: The Fall of Jericho
6.context: Jericho's walls collapse — Israel wins not by weapons but by seven days of marching and a single shout. The first conquest battle is God's work.

24.title: The Covenant Renewed at Shechem
24.context: Joshua's final covenant renewal at Shechem — and his famous personal declaration: 'As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.'

1.title: Israel Fails to Complete the Conquest

4.title: Deborah and Barak
4.context: Deborah — the only female judge — and Jael team up to defeat Sisera. The story celebrates God using unexpected people for unexpected victories.

6.title: Gideon Called
6.context: Gideon — a fearful farmer hiding from raiders — is called 'mighty warrior' by God. What God sees in us is greater than what we see in ourselves.

1.title: Ruth's Pledge
1.context: 'Your people will be my people and your God my God.' A Moabite woman pledges her life — and ends up the great-grandmother of King David.

1.title: The Birth of Samuel
1.context: Hannah's barren grief and desperate prayer give birth to Samuel. The story whispers what God will say openly: he hears broken hearts.

3.title: The LORD Calls Samuel
3.context: 'Speak, LORD, your servant is listening.' Young Samuel's reply has shaped the prayer of faithful believers ever since.

8.title: Israel Demands a King
8.context: The people demand a human king — rejecting not Samuel but God himself. God grants the request, but warns what kings will cost them.

16.title: David Anointed
16.context: God chooses David — the youngest, overlooked son. 'Man looks at the outside; the LORD looks at the heart.' One of the Bible's central truths.

17.title: David and Goliath
17.context: David and Goliath — a boy with a sling defeats a giant. The story has become the universal symbol of faith taking on the impossible.

28.title: Saul and the Medium of Endor

1.title: David's Lament for Saul and Jonathan

7.title: God's Covenant with David
7.context: The Davidic covenant — God promises David an eternal throne. The fountainhead of every messianic prophecy. Every NT 'Son of David' title flows from here.

11.title: David and Bathsheba
11.context: David's greatest failure — adultery with Bathsheba, murder of Uriah. The Bible never sanitizes its heroes. It tells the truth.

3.title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
3.context: Solomon asks for wisdom rather than wealth — and becomes the model for 'asking for the right thing' for three millennia.

8.title: The Ark Brought to the Temple

13.title: The Man of God from Judah

18.title: Confrontation at Mount Carmel
18.context: The showdown at Mount Carmel — Elijah alone against 450 prophets of Baal. God answers with fire, and the people cry: 'The LORD, he is God!'

19.title: Elijah Flees to Horeb
19.context: After his greatest victory, Elijah crashes into despair. God meets him not in wind or fire but in 'a still small voice' — comfort for every weary servant.

2.title: Elijah Taken Up to Heaven
2.context: Elijah taken up by chariots of fire — one of only two figures in Scripture who never tasted death. Elisha receives a double portion of the Spirit.

5.title: Naaman Healed
5.context: Naaman, a foreign general, has to swallow his pride and dip seven times in the Jordan. Jesus cites the story to show God's mercy reaches beyond Israel.

22.title: The Book of the Law Found

34.title: The Book of the Law Found

4.title: For Such a Time as This

8.title: The King's Edict for the Jews

38.title: The LORD Speaks from the Whirlwind

1.title: The Way of the Righteous
1.context: The doorway to the Psalms. Two paths, two destinies — and the wise are those who delight in God's instruction day and night.

2.title: The Reign of the Lord's Anointed
2.context: A messianic coronation psalm quoted repeatedly in the New Testament. The kings of earth rage in vain against the Anointed One God himself has installed.

8.title: God's Glory and Human Dignity
8.context: A meditation under the stars: 'What is man that you are mindful of him?' Quoted in Hebrews 2 to describe Christ — the true Son of Man.

15.title: Who Shall Dwell on Your Holy Hill?

20.title: Trust in the Name of the LORD

22.title: From Suffering to Praise
22.context: The cry Jesus echoed from the cross. Centuries before Calvary, David describes pierced hands and feet, mocking onlookers, and gambling for clothing.

23.title: The LORD Is My Shepherd
23.context: Perhaps the most beloved chapter in all Scripture. Through danger, fear, and even the valley of death's shadow, the believer is shepherded — not abandoned.

27.title: The LORD My Light
27.context: 'The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?' A psalm of bold trust spoken into the darkness.

31.title: Into Your Hand I Commit My Spirit

34.title: Taste and See the LORD Is Good

37.title: Do Not Fret Because of Evildoers

41.title: Blessed Is He Who Considers the Poor

42.title: As the Deer Pants for Water
42.context: 'As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul pants for you, O God.' A psalm of depression that still preaches to its own soul.

46.title: God Is Our Refuge
46.context: 'God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.' Martin Luther's 'A Mighty Fortress' draws its language from this psalm.

47.title: God the King of All Earth

49.title: The Folly of Trusting in Riches

51.title: Create in Me a Clean Heart
51.context: David's cry of repentance after his sin with Bathsheba. Every fallen believer who has dared to hope in God's mercy finds words here.

73.title: The Tempting Prosperity of the Wicked

84.title: How Lovely Is Your Dwelling Place

90.title: God Is Eternal
90.context: A psalm of Moses — a meditation on life's brevity. 'Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.'

91.title: The Shelter of the Most High
91.context: A psalm of the safest of all places — under the shadow of the Almighty. Satan misquoted these lines tempting Jesus in the wilderness.

97.title: The LORD Reigns, Let the Earth Rejoice

98.title: Sing a New Song to the LORD

99.title: The LORD Our God Is Holy

100.title: A Psalm of Thanksgiving
100.context: A bright song of universal worship. For a thousand years, Christian congregations have begun their services with these joyful lines.

103.title: Bless the LORD, O My Soul

106.title: The LORD's Steadfast Love and Israel's Rebellion

108.title: Through God We Shall Do Valiantly

109.title: Help Me, O LORD My God

110.title: The Lord Says to My Lord

113.title: Praise the Name of the LORD

114.title: When Israel Came Out of Egypt

119.title: The Word of God: A Meditation
119.context: The longest chapter in the Bible — 176 verses in 22 alphabetic sections — a sustained meditation on the beauty and life-giving power of God's word.

121.title: My Help Comes from the LORD
121.context: 'I lift up my eyes to the hills — where does my help come from? My help comes from the LORD.' The most beloved of the pilgrim psalms.

122.title: Pray for the Peace of Jerusalem

123.title: Our Eyes Look to the LORD

124.title: If the LORD Had Not Been on Our Side

125.title: Those Who Trust in the LORD

128.title: Blessed Is Everyone Who Fears the LORD

130.title: Out of the Depths
130.context: 'Out of the depths I cry to you, O LORD.' The penitential psalm Luther called 'a Pauline psalm' — every line drips with grace.

139.title: God Knows Me Completely
139.context: The Bible's deepest meditation on divine omniscience. There is no height, depth, or darkness where God's hand cannot reach the believer.

143.title: Lead Me in the Way I Should Go

146.title: Praise the LORD, O My Soul

150.title: Praise the LORD with All Instruments
150.context: The final psalm — pure, distilled praise. From the deepest lament (Psalm 22) to the highest acclamation (Psalm 150), all of life ends in worship.

31.title: The Wife of Noble Character
31.context: The 'wife of noble character' — written as a Hebrew acrostic. The summation of Proverbs' picture of skillful, godly living.

3.title: A Time for Everything
3.context: 'For everything there is a season.' A meditation on life's rhythms — a reminder that God reigns over every season we live through.

12.title: Remember Your Creator
12.context: The book's peak: 'Remember your Creator in the days of your youth.' Then a stunning poetic portrait of aging and death.

6.title: Isaiah's Call
6.context: Isaiah's call vision — God on the throne, seraphim crying 'Holy, holy, holy.' One encounter that reshapes the rest of his life.

9.title: A Child Is Born to Us
9.context: 'For unto us a child is born…' The classic Christmas text — and one of the Old Testament's most explicit messianic titles for Jesus.

11.title: The Reign of Jesse's Branch
11.context: The messianic 'Branch from Jesse's root' — a recurring image in Isaiah, fulfilled in Jesus, son of David, son of Jesse.

40.title: Comfort My People
40.context: Isaiah pivots from judgment to comfort: 'Comfort my people.' The New Testament uses these very words to introduce John the Baptist.

53.title: He Was Pierced for Our Transgressions
53.context: Written 700 years before Calvary — the most detailed prophecy of substitutionary atonement in the Old Testament. Every line maps onto Christ's cross.

65.title: New Heavens and New Earth
65.context: 'Behold, I create new heavens and a new earth.' Isaiah voices the Bible's greatest hope — fulfilled in Revelation 21.

1.title: The Call of Jeremiah
1.context: Jeremiah called before he was even born: 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you.' A powerful reminder that God's calling precedes our awareness.

31.title: The New Covenant
31.context: The new covenant prophecy. Hebrews 8 quotes it in full, declaring it fulfilled in Christ — the law written on the heart, sin remembered no more.

3.title: His Mercies Are New
3.context: At the heart of the city's grief stands one of Scripture's greatest declarations of grace: 'His mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning.'

36.title: A New Heart
36.context: 'I will give you a new heart… I will put my Spirit within you.' The Old Testament's clearest preview of Pentecost — and the heart of New Covenant living.

37.title: The Valley of Dry Bones
37.context: The valley of dry bones — can a destroyed nation live again? God's answer: yes, by my Word and my Spirit. The image still speaks today.

3.title: The Fiery Furnace
3.context: Three young men refuse to bow to a golden image. Their faith reads 'God can save us — but even if he does not, we will not bow.' One of Scripture's bravest moments.

6.title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
6.context: Daniel in the lions' den — already an old man, still praying three times a day toward Jerusalem. Loyalty over self-preservation.

7.title: Vision of the Four Beasts
7.context: 'One like a son of man' coming on the clouds — Daniel's deepest preview of Christ. Jesus' favorite self-designation comes straight from this vision.

9.title: Daniel's Prayer and the Seventy Sevens
9.context: Daniel reads Jeremiah's prophecy and his prayer awakens. This prophet teaches us how to pray Scripture's promises back to God.

11.title: Kings of the South and North

1.title: Jonah Flees
1.context: Jonah doesn't flee the mission — he flees God's mercy. He doesn't want Nineveh to repent. Perhaps the Bible's most honest prophet.

1.title: In the Belly of the Fish

3.title: Jonah Preaches in Nineveh
3.context: Nineveh repents — pagan Assyrians outdo God's own people in turning from sin. Jesus cites Jonah as a sign of his own resurrection (Matt 12:40).

5.title: A Ruler from Bethlehem
5.context: Under the shadow of exile, Micah names Bethlehem — the small town where the Messiah will be born. Cited in Matthew 2 to Herod's wise men.

2.title: The Righteous Live by Faith
2.context: 'The righteous shall live by his faith' — quoted three times in the New Testament. The seedbed of the Reformation's central doctrine.

9.title: The Coming King
9.context: 'Behold, your king comes… humble and riding on a donkey.' Prophesied 500 years before Palm Sunday — fulfilled to the letter in Matthew 21.

4.title: The Sun of Righteousness
4.context: The Old Testament's final prophecy: Elijah will come. John the Baptist fulfills it (Matt 11:14). Then 400 years of silence — until the angel speaks to Zechariah in Luke 1.

1.title: The Genealogy of Jesus
1.context: Matthew opens with a genealogy because identity matters. Jesus is shown to fulfill both the Abrahamic promise of blessing and the Davidic promise of an eternal King.

3.title: John the Baptist Prepares the Way

5.title: The Sermon on the Mount: The Beatitudes
5.context: Jesus' foundational sermon, delivered early in his Galilean ministry. The Beatitudes invert worldly values — calling the poor in spirit, the mourners, and the persecuted 'blessed'.

5.title: Salt and Light
5.context: Salt and light — Jesus' core declaration of disciple identity. Not a command but a statement of fact: you ARE these things; now live like it.

6.title: The Lord's Prayer
6.context: The pattern Jesus gave his disciples for prayer. Every line is a window into the heart of how citizens of the kingdom relate to their Father.

6.title: Do Not Worry
6.context: 'Do not be anxious' — Jesus says it three times. If your Father feeds the birds, will he not also feed you?

9.title: The Dead Girl and the Sick Woman
Jesus Heals the Blind and Mute

13.title: The Parable of the Sower
13.context: The kingdom parables — Jesus reveals heavenly mysteries through earthly stories. Chapter 7 was the teacher; this chapter is the storyteller.

14.title: Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand
14.context: After hearing of John the Baptist's death, Jesus withdraws — but the crowd follows. He feeds 5,000 with five loaves and two fish.

15.title: The Faith of the Canaanite Woman

16.title: Peter's Confession of Christ
16.context: Peter's confession at Caesarea Philippi is the hinge of all four Gospels. After this moment, Jesus begins openly teaching that he must die and rise again.

17.title: The Transfiguration
17.context: On a mountain, Jesus' divine glory briefly breaks through his humanity. Moses (Law) and Elijah (Prophets) appear with him — both pointing to the One greater than themselves.

18.title: The Parable of the Lost Sheep
Dealing with Sin in the Church
The Parable of the Unforgiving Servant

21.title: The Triumphal Entry
21.context: Palm Sunday — Jesus enters Jerusalem riding a donkey, fulfilling Zechariah 9:9. A public declaration: I am the messianic King.

21.title: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants

22.title: The Parable of the Wedding Banquet

24.title: Signs of the End of the Age
No One Knows the Day or Hour

25.title: The Parable of the Ten Virgins
The Final Judgment
25.context: The final judgment — Jesus judges by how we treated 'the least of these.' Faith is real when it shows up at the side of the suffering.

26.title: The Last Supper
26.context: Jesus' final Passover. By breaking bread and pouring the cup, he institutes the new covenant in his body and blood — a memorial the church keeps to this day.

26.title: Gethsemane
26.context: In Gethsemane, the fully human Jesus wrestles with the cup before him — and submits to the Father's will. The hour of redemption begins here.

27.title: The Crucifixion
27.context: The crucifixion — the most public execution in history. The Gospels treat it with strange restraint, letting the event speak for itself.

28.title: The Resurrection
28.context: The climax of the New Testament. The resurrection vindicates Jesus' atoning sacrifice and inaugurates the hope of eternal life for all who trust him.

28.title: The Great Commission
28.context: The Great Commission. The risen Jesus sends his disciples to all nations — the marching orders that have driven 2,000 years of Christian mission.

1.title: John the Baptist Prepares the Way
1.context: Mark moves at breakneck speed — the shortest, most action-packed Gospel. The opening line states the thesis: Jesus is the Son of God.

1.title: Jesus Casts Out an Evil Spirit
Jesus Prays in a Solitary Place
Jesus Heals a Man with Leprosy

4.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
4.context: Jesus stills a storm. The terrified disciples ask the question Mark wants every reader to ask: 'Who is this, that even the wind and sea obey him?'

5.title: A Dead Girl and a Sick Woman
5.context: Two desperate stories interlock: the synagogue ruler's daughter and the bleeding woman. Jesus has time for both — the prominent and the outcast.

7.title: The Faith of a Syrophoenician Woman
Jesus Heals a Deaf and Mute Man

8.title: Healing the Blind Man at Bethsaida
Peter's Confession of Christ
8.context: Mark's hinge. The first eight chapters answer 'Who is Jesus?' Peter's confession unlocks the second half: 'What did he come to do?' — to suffer and die.

9.title: The Transfiguration
9.context: The Transfiguration — Jesus' divine glory breaks through, with Moses (Law) and Elijah (Prophets) appearing alongside. The veil lifts for one moment.

9.title: Jesus Heals a Boy with an Evil Spirit

10.title: Jesus Predicts His Death a Third Time
The Request of James and John

11.title: Cursing the Fig Tree and Clearing the Temple

13.title: Signs of the End of the Age

14.title: Gethsemane
14.context: Gethsemane — Jesus' full humanity wrestles with the cup before him, but yields: 'Not my will, but yours be done.' The hour of redemption begins.

16.title: Jesus Has Risen
16.context: The foundation of Christian faith. Mark's brief account is full of eyewitness texture — running, fear, breathlessness — the sound of life-altering news.

2.title: The Birth of Jesus
2.context: The birth of Jesus — in the middle of a Roman census, the Messiah is born outside a Bethlehem inn. God's story unfolds in real history.

2.title: Jesus at Twelve in the Temple

4.title: The Temptation
4.context: Jesus, baptized, is led into the wilderness — forty days mirroring Israel's forty years. The Second Adam succeeds where the first Israel failed.

10.title: The Good Samaritan
10.context: The Good Samaritan — Jesus shatters racial prejudice, redefining 'neighbor' as anyone in need. The hated foreigner becomes the hero.

15.title: Lost and Found
15.context: Three parables of lost things found — sheep, coin, son. Each shows God actively seeking and joyfully receiving. The heart of the gospel in story form.

19.title: Zacchaeus
19.context: Zacchaeus — chief tax collector of Jericho, despised by all. Jesus invites himself to dinner. 'The Son of Man came to seek and save the lost.'

24.title: On the Road to Emmaus
24.context: On the road to Emmaus — two discouraged disciples meet the risen Christ, who shows them how all of Scripture points to himself.

1.title: The Word Became Flesh
1.context: John mirrors Genesis with his opening: 'In the beginning was the Word.' The eternal Logos — through whom all things were made — has now become flesh.

3.title: Jesus Teaches Nicodemus
3.context: A leading Pharisee comes by night for an encounter that contains the most-quoted verse in the Bible (3:16) — and a teaching that has changed millions of lives.

4.title: The Samaritan Woman at the Well
4.context: Jesus crosses every boundary — racial, gender, religious — to offer 'living water' to a Samaritan woman at a well. By chapter's end, her village believes.

6.title: Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand
6.context: Feeding the 5,000 — the only miracle (besides the resurrection) recorded in all four Gospels. John uses it to open the 'I am the bread of life' discourse.

8.title: The Woman Caught in Adultery
8.context: The woman caught in adultery — 'Let any one of you who is without sin cast the first stone.' One of Jesus' most famous defenses of mercy.

8.title: Jesus the Light of the World
The Truth Will Set You Free

9.title: Jesus Heals a Man Born Blind
9.context: A man born blind sees — but the climax is not physical sight but spiritual vision. 'Lord, I believe.' Both eyes finally open.

10.title: The Good Shepherd
10.context: 'I am the good shepherd' — Jesus echoes Ezekiel 34's rebuke of failed shepherds and steps into the role himself. The Lord is my shepherd.

11.title: The Death and Raising of Lazarus
11.context: The most dramatic miracle in John's Gospel. Raising Lazarus — dead four days — both ignites Jesus' final week and previews his own resurrection.

13.title: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
13.context: On the night of his betrayal, the King washes his disciples' feet — overturning every worldly notion of power and service in a single act.

14.title: I Am the Way, Truth, and Life
14.context: On the night of his betrayal, Jesus comforts his frightened disciples: 'I am the way, the truth, and the life.' Words still anchoring believers today.

14.title: The Promise of the Holy Spirit

15.title: The True Vine
15.context: 'I am the true vine' — Jesus uses Israel's classic self-image to describe the life-union between himself and his followers.

16.title: The Work of the Holy Spirit
The Disciples' Grief Will Turn to Joy

17.title: Jesus Prays for Himself and His Disciples
17.context: Jesus' high priestly prayer — interceding for his disciples and for every believer who would come after them. The deepest prayer in the New Testament.

20.title: The Empty Tomb
20.context: The empty tomb — the foundation of the Christian faith. John records the details of what he himself saw with the precision of an eyewitness.

21.title: Jesus and the Miraculous Catch of Fish

1.title: Jesus Taken Up Into Heaven
1.context: Acts is volume two of Luke's Gospel. After Jesus' ascension, the Spirit propels his followers from Jerusalem to Rome — and the church begins.

2.title: The Holy Spirit Comes at Pentecost
2.context: Pentecost fulfills Jesus' promise. The Spirit descends, the Gospel is preached in many tongues, and 3,000 are added to the church in a single day.

4.title: Peter and John Before the Sanhedrin

7.title: The Stoning of Stephen
7.context: Stephen's martyrdom — the church's first martyr. As stones rain down, a young man named Saul looks on. The persecutor will become an apostle.

8.title: Philip and the Ethiopian
8.context: Philip and the Ethiopian — the gospel reaches Africa explicitly. A high official reading Isaiah 53 finds his answer in Christ.

9.title: Saul's Conversion
9.context: The church's chief persecutor encounters the risen Christ on the Damascus road. Saul of Tarsus becomes Paul the apostle — a hinge moment in history.

10.title: Cornelius Calls for Peter
10.context: Through twin visions, God orchestrates Peter's visit to the Gentile centurion Cornelius. The Gospel is officially opened to the nations.

10.title: The Holy Spirit Comes Upon the Gentiles

15.title: The Council at Jerusalem
15.context: The Jerusalem Council settles the church's most divisive question: Gentile believers do not have to keep the Mosaic law to be saved. The unity of the church is preserved.

16.title: Paul's Vision of the Man of Macedonia
Lydia's Conversion in Philippi
16.context: Lydia believes — the first seed of European Christianity. A businesswoman in Philippi opens her home and her family enters the kingdom.

17.title: Paul's Speech at the Areopagus
17.context: Paul's masterful sermon to Greek philosophers at the Areopagus. He starts with their own poets and altars and ends with the resurrection of Christ.

20.title: Paul's Farewell to the Ephesian Elders

27.title: Paul Sails for Rome
27.context: Paul's voyage to Rome — a prisoner becomes the calmest man on a sinking ship. One of the most accurate ancient sea-voyage narratives anywhere.

28.title: Paul Preaches at Rome Under Guard

1.title: The Power of the Gospel
1.context: Paul's thesis: 'I am not ashamed of the Gospel — it is the power of God for salvation.' Everything in Romans unpacks this single sentence.

3.title: Righteousness Through Faith
3.context: The heart of Romans — and arguably the heart of the Gospel. God's righteousness is revealed apart from the law and received through faith in Christ alone.

5.title: Peace and Hope
5.context: The fruits of justification: peace with God, access to grace, hope, and the strange gift of suffering — which produces the very character we long for.

6.title: Dead to Sin, Alive in Christ

8.title: Life Through the Spirit
8.context: One of the highest peaks in Scripture. 'No condemnation' opens the chapter; 'no separation' closes it. In between: the Spirit, suffering, and unshakable hope.

12.title: A Living Sacrifice
12.context: The pivot from doctrine to ethics. In view of God's mercy, we offer ourselves as living sacrifices — and the rest of life flows from that response.

11.title: The Lord's Supper
11.context: Paul corrects abuses of the Lord's Supper at Corinth. The meal proclaims Christ's death until he comes — a constant rehearsal of the gospel.

13.title: The Way of Love
13.context: The love chapter — read at countless weddings, but originally written to a divided church to remind them love is the only true mark of being Spirit-filled.

15.title: The Resurrection of Christ
15.context: The resurrection chapter — the foundation of Christian faith. 'If Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile.' The most fundamental defense in Scripture.

4.title: Treasure in Jars of Clay
4.context: 'We have this treasure in jars of clay' — Paul's deepest portrait of ministry: fragile vessels carrying eternal glory.

12.title: Paul's Vision and Thorn
12.context: Paul's thorn in the flesh — three times he begs God to remove it. The answer: 'My grace is sufficient for you. My power is made perfect in weakness.'

3.title: By Faith, Like Abraham
3.context: Paul's exasperated cry: 'You foolish Galatians!' The argument that justification comes by faith and faith alone — an argument that fired the Reformation.

5.title: The Fruit of the Spirit
5.context: The fruit of the Spirit — nine traits that mark the Spirit-shaped life. Not nine separate fruits, but one fruit with nine flavors of Christlikeness.

2.title: From Death to Life
2.context: 'You were dead in your transgressions and sins… but God made us alive with Christ.' Paul's most striking picture of salvation as resurrection.

6.title: The Armor of God
6.context: The armor of God — the Christian's struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against spiritual forces. Paul's battle gear is mostly defensive.

2.title: Christ's Humility
2.context: The Christ-hymn — the New Testament's most condensed declaration of who Jesus is and what he did. Likely an early church hymn Paul incorporated.

4.title: Anxious for Nothing
4.context: 'Do not be anxious about anything, but pray about everything.' A prison letter's prescription for peace — written by a man in chains.

1.title: The Supremacy of Christ
1.context: The Colossian Christ-hymn — declaring Christ as creator, sustainer, head of the church, and reconciler of all things. Christology in poetic compression.

6.title: Slaves and the Love of Money

1.title: Receive Him as You Would Me
God Has Spoken by His Son

4.title: Our Great High Priest
4.context: 'Our great high priest' — the heart of Hebrews. Jesus fully understands our weakness AND lives forever to intercede for us. The best of both.

11.title: By Faith
11.context: The 'hall of faith' — from Abel to Moses to the unnamed sufferers. 'The world was not worthy of them.' A roll-call of those who lived by faith.

12.title: Looking to Jesus
12.context: 'Run with endurance the race set before us' — Hebrews' pastoral climax. Look to Jesus, who endured the cross for the joy set before him.

1.title: Trials and Wisdom
1.context: James opens with a paradox: count trials all joy. Why? Because they produce the very steadfastness that completes faith.

2.title: Faith Without Works Is Dead
2.context: 'Faith without works is dead' — James's central thesis. Not contradicting Paul's 'justified by faith' but completing it: real faith always works.

3.title: Taming the Tongue
3.context: The tongue — James's vivid warning about the destructive power of speech: fire, poison, an untamable beast hanging in our jaws.

1.title: Born to a Living Hope
1.context: Peter writes to 'exiles scattered abroad' — every Christian's true identity. Our home is not here; we live as resident aliens until Christ returns.

2.title: A Chosen People
2.context: 'You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood' — Exodus 19's words for Israel are now spoken over the church. We inherit Sinai through Christ.

4.title: Sharing in Christ's Sufferings
4.context: 'Do not be surprised at the fiery trial.' Suffering is part of Christian life, not an interruption to it. Peter — soon to die for Christ — knows this firsthand.

3.title: The Day of the Lord
3.context: Why does the Lord delay? 'He is patient with you, not wishing that any should perish.' What looks like silence is actually mercy.

4.title: God Is Love
4.context: 'God is love' — one of two of Scripture's deepest declarations of God's essence (the other: 'God is spirit', John 4:24).

1.title: Revelation of Jesus Christ
1.context: Revelation opens — exiled John on Patmos receives visions that pull back the curtain on cosmic history. The Bible's most symbolic book begins.

4.title: The Throne in Heaven
4.context: The throne vision — beneath all the chaos of history, God still reigns. Heaven's first response is worship: 'Holy, holy, holy.'

5.title: The Lamb Worthy
5.context: The Lamb opens the seals — only 'the Lamb who was slain' is worthy. The key to all history is the cross.

10.title: The Angel and the Little Scroll

19.title: The Rider on the White Horse
19.context: The rider on the white horse — Christ's triumphant return. The New Testament begins with a manger and ends with a throne.

21.title: A New Heaven and Earth
21.context: 'A new heaven and a new earth' — the Bible's deepest hope fulfilled. God dwells with his people; tears, death, and pain are undone forever.

22.title: I Am Coming Soon
22.context: Scripture's final promise: 'Behold, I am coming soon!' The church's two-millennium response: 'Come, Lord Jesus.'
